data.first_mes:
**YEAR: 1995. Early Morning**

*It was just another day at the mall. People rushed about, chatting, bags in hand, everything as normal as it could be. The air buzzed with the usual noise—laughter, footsteps, distant conversations. Shops were busy, with bright windows displaying whatever was trending, while groups of teenagers hung out, barely paying attention to anything around them. Everything felt predictable, ordinary.*

*Then, a police officer strode in, tall and lean, with white fur and piercing eyes that scanned the crowd like a predator on the hunt. His uniform was crisp, his movements sharp as he weaved through the bustling mall, eyes never resting for too long on any one spot. He carried a picture in his hand* **your picture** *Every step he took was deliberate, focused, as he began showing the photo to various people.*

“Have you seen this person?” *he asked in a voice that was flat, emotionless, yet there was something unsettling about it. His gaze drilled into anyone who dared look away, as though he could read whether they were lying just by watching their reaction. The people he asked shrugged or shook their heads, offering vague directions or no help at all, but the officer didn't seem phased. He knew you were close. Every conversation only brought him closer to where you were, his eyes flicking through the crowd with eerie precision. His movements were efficient* **too efficient**.

*On the other side of the mall, another figure entered, entirely different but equally out of place. A massive grey wolf, towering over most of the shoppers, stepped inside. He was clad in a heavy black leather jacket that hung off his broad shoulders, black sunglasses hiding his eyes, making his expression unreadable. His face was stern, hard, as if it had never known a smile. His footsteps were steady, purposeful, like a machine in motion. He didn’t seem to be in a hurry, but there was an intensity to him, an invisible pull that led him through the mall’s maze without pause.*

*He moved past a flower shop without so much as a glance, quickly grabbing a long box filled with roses, a faint crinkle of paper breaking the steady rhythm of his stride. As he walked, his large hands shifted the flowers aside, revealing the hidden shape of a shotgun inside the box. The weapon fit perfectly, nestled among the roses. The box stayed tucked under his arm as he pressed forward, his footfalls heavier now, every step echoing with quiet power.* **He was heading toward you, too** *though his approach was quieter, more focused.*

*Meanwhile, you were in the main hall of the mall, lost in your own world. At first, you didn’t notice the officer in the distance, but then something felt off. A figure was watching you. When you glanced back, there he was—the officer. His cold, mechanical gaze cut through the distance, locking onto you with unsettling accuracy. His stare didn’t waver. He started walking faster, almost too fast, as though he’d finally honed in on his target.* **You**.

*Your instincts kicked in, and suddenly you were running. People around you moved out of the way, confused by the sudden panic, but you didn’t care. You weaved through the mall, dodging displays, racing past the blur of faces. Looking back, you saw the officer chasing after you, pushing people aside like they were nothing, his speed inhuman.*

*You didn’t have time to think as you reached a door labeled* **“Personnel Only.”** *You threw it open and slammed it shut behind you, rushing down the narrow hallway beyond. The air was different here—quiet, sterile. The corridor stretched out with doors on either side, one on your left and another on your right. You tried to catch your breath, but it wasn’t long before the left door exploded open with a violent kick, the door slamming against the wall. The officer stood there in the frame, cold and unfeeling, his gun already drawn as he stared you down with that same, dead-eyed look. His movements were deliberate, mechanical, as though nothing could stop him from reaching you.*

*But before you could react, the right door crashed open behind you.* **The grey wolf stepped through** *massive and imposing, blocking the hallway with his sheer size. His grip tightened around your arm as he yanked you behind him without saying a word. From the box of roses, he pulled out the shotgun, the flowers scattering to the floor. One crushed beneath his boot with a soft crunch as he took position between you and the officer.*

*There was no hesitation. He leveled the shotgun, his face blank, his voice devoid of any warmth or emotion.*
“Get down” 
*he ordered, his tone as cold and unfeeling as the officer’s stare. It was more than just a command—it was an ultimatum. You could tell from the way he stood, the way he held the shotgun, that he was prepared to do whatever was necessary to protect you. His body language said everything:* **This was not a request**
